Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The failing test `testQuinticMin` in the `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizerTest` class is calling the `getResult` method of `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer`. The bug report suggests that the `getResult` method in `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer` returns the result of the last run of the underlying optimizer, which might not be the best one.

Looking at the `getResult` method in `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer`, it simply delegates to the `getResult` method of the `optimizer`. This means that the `getResult` method of `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer` is returning the result of the last run of the underlying optimizer without any additional logic to select the best result.

To fix this issue, the `getResult` method in `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer` should be modified to select the best result from multiple runs of the optimizer rather than just returning the result of the last run.

Next, I will identify the location where the `getResult` method should be fixed.

messages.content:
" Get all the optima found during the last call to {@link * #optimize(UnivariateRealFunction, GoalType, double, double) optimize}. *

The optimizer stores all the optima found during a set of * restarts. The {@link #optimize(UnivariateRealFunction, GoalType, * double, double) optimize} method returns the best point only. This * method returns all the points found at the end of each starts, * including the best one already returned by the {@link * #optimize(UnivariateRealFunction, GoalType, double, double) optimize} * method. *

*

* The returned array as one element for each start as specified * in the constructor. It is ordered with the results from the * runs that did converge first, sorted from best to worst * objective value (i.e in ascending order if minimizing and in * descending order if maximizing), followed by Double.NaN elements * corresponding to the runs that did not converge. This means all * elements will be NaN if the {@link #optimize(UnivariateRealFunction, * GoalType, double, double) optimize} method did throw a {@link * ConvergenceException ConvergenceException}). This also means that * if the first element is not NaN, it is the best point found across * all starts.

* @return array containing the optima * @exception IllegalStateException if {@link #optimize(UnivariateRealFunction, * GoalType, double, double) optimize} has not been called * @see #getOptimaValues() "

* @return array containing the optima * @exception IllegalStateException if {@link #optimize(UnivariateRealFunction, * GoalType, double, double) optimize} has not been called * @see #getOptima() "

The `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer` class has two methods related to retrieving the optima found during optimization runs:
1. `getOptima`: Returns an array containing the optima found during the last call to the `optimize` method. It ensures that the best point found across all starts is returned as the first element of the array.
2. `getOptimaValues`: Returns an array containing the function values at optima found during the last call to the `optimize` method. Similar to `getOptima`, it ensures that the best point found across all starts is returned as the first element of the array.

The bug report suggests that the current behavior of `getResult` in `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer` might not return the best result from multiple runs of the optimizer. To address this issue, the logic for selecting the best result should be updated in the `getResult` method of `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer`.

Based on the functionalities provided by `getOptima` and `getOptimaValues`, a possible fix for the issue in `getResult` could involve selecting the best result from the array returned by `getOptima` or `getOptimaValues`.

Next, I will suggest the methods that would be the best locations to implement the fix.
The following methods would be the best locations to implement the fix:
1. `org.apache.commons.math.optimization.MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer.getResult()` 

These methods are where the logic to select the best result from multiple runs of the optimizer can be implemented to ensure that `getResult` returns the best result.
